chunks: I read a letter from a man to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'A man was born upon Islam, then he disbelieved, associated partners [with God], and exited from Islam. Is he repelled [to be repented] or is he killed and not repelled?' He wrote: 'He is killed.' As for the woman when she apostatizes, she is not killed in any case, but she is confined to prison indefinitely if she does not return to Islam. And this was included in the narration of Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from more than one [narrator] from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and it adds clarification to that.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for male and female apostates in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinct jurisprudential treatment of male and female apostates, ruling that males are subject to execution (qatl) regardless of whether they are given a chance to repent, while females are not executed but rather imprisoned (mu'allaqah) until they return to Islam. This ruling is supported by earlier traditions from Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq, as cited by al--Tusi, highlighting the established Shia position on the gender-specific application of the death penalty for apostasy.
